title: Mined public X pairs with a one-word delta, grouped stored-leaf birthday search

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold algorithm of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 over the challenge and fresh coins: one fresh 64-bit coin opens the run with probability K/2^64, K = 7203743407894960820, the least integer with (K/2^64) lo_run >= 0.39, lo_run the exact opened-run bound of success.md 6.5 (every abort, drop, cap, defect and the fixup meter charged as failure rows). Its expected total work is at most 2^123.394722300424726 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit), 2^7 + (K/2^64) E_run, an opened run's expected work at most 70.1365 per leaf (success.md 6.6); the worst case, 2^190.446050 instructions, is disclosed. The run first mines 2^14 pairs of public points [s]P whose y^2 differ by less than 2^63 (Phase 0, charged, capped; aborts with no padding branch on proof.md 2.3's tests), then runs proof.md's grouped stored-leaf birthday search with those X's. Peak memory at most 2^135.9802 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^117.8900 units, Phase 0 included; no advice; certificate.py checks every declared figure. No prior acceptance or score is a premise. An analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Kernels, sites, fixups, labels, ygen and both hops (4 x 4 machine) against bit-exact models; Phase 0; the resolver; every kernel count against certificate.py, which it runs (proof.md 8). Not a production-scale attack.
